newsitem.title: CANADA: Loewen closes Rose Hills acquisition.
newsitem.headline: Loewen closes Rose Hills acquisition.

text.p: The Loewen Group Inc said Wednesday it closed the US$240 million acquisition of the Rose Hills cemetery in Los Angeles in partnership with New York investment group Blackstone Capital Partners II Merchant Banking Fund LP.

Loewen, North America's second-biggest funeral home operator, will have a 20.5 percent stake in the property at first with an option to buy out Blackstone after four years. Loewen contributed US$95 million in cash and property and Blackstone contributed US$35 million in equity to fund the deal.
The rest of the money came from bank debt syndicated by Goldman Sachs and Bank of Nova Scotia and 9.5 percent senior subordinated notes issued by Rose Hills and syndicated by Smith Barney.
Kendall Nungesser, chief financial officer of the firm formerly owning the cemetery, was named president and chief executive officer of Rose Hills Co.
The newly formed company will hold the Rose Hills cemetery and mortuary along with 14 funeral homes and two combination funeral homes and cemeteries already owned by Loewen in the Los Angeles area.
Dennis Poulsen, former president and chief executive officer of Rose Hills, will be chairman of the new company.
In addition to the two executives, the board will include two Loewen representatives and three Blackstone representatives.

Loewen reiterated that it expects the deal to be accretive to earnings per share. The partnership with Blackston enabled it to avoid issueing shares to pay for the transaction "at a price the company considers undervalued." Service Corp International, which has announced a US$2.9 billion hostile bid for Loewen, has criticized the Rose Hills deal.
